study type: Secondary analyses of a randomized controlled trial
outcome: development of a niche in the uterine scar
cohort: The study included women undergoing a first caesarean section in 32 hospitals in the Netherlands.
finding: The developed prognostic prediction model for niche development after a first CS showed poor discriminative ability (median AUC ranged from 0.56 to 0.62) and cannot be used accurately, though factors like gestational age, twin pregnancy, smoking, double-layer closure, surgical experience, multiparity, and suture material were identified as influencing scar healing.
mod_finding: Surgical technique factors during the caesarean section, such as double-layer closure, surgical experience, and suture material (Vicryl), were found to influence scar healing and niche development, and the model for elective CS yielded similar results.
